problem: Which of the following is a factor of $-{v}^{2}+12v-45?$

examples.knowledge_point: Factoring a Quadratic Polynomial With Complex Roots
examples.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(u) = u^2-2u+10.$

Next, we solve $f(u) = 0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(u) & =0 \\ {u}^{2}-2u+10 & =0 \\ ({u}^{2}-2u+{1}^{2})-{1}^{2}+10 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2}-1+10 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2}+9 & =0 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =-9 \\ (u-1)^{2} & =9{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (u-1)^{2} & =(3\text{i})^{2} \\ u-1 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ u & =1\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since our quadratic equation has roots $u_1=1+ 3\textrm{i}$ and $u_2=1- 3\textrm{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ the expression $u^2-2u+10$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-2u+10 & =a(u-{u}_{1})(u-{u}_{2}) \\  & =(u-(1+3\text{i}))(u-(1-3\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(y)$ has real coefficients, has roots ${y}_{1}=4+\text{i}$ and ${y}_{2}=4-\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $2.$ Find $f(y).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${y}_{1}=4+\text{i}$ and ${y}_{2}=4-\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(y-{y}_{1})(y-{y}_{2}) & =2(y-(4+\text{i}))(y-(4-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(y-(4+\text{i}))(y-(4-\text{i})) & =2({y}^{2}-(4+\text{i})y-(4-\text{i})y+(4+\text{i})(4-\text{i})) \\  & =2({y}^{2}-(4+\text{i}+4-\text{i})y+({4}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2})) \\  & =2({y}^{2}-8y+(16+1)) \\  & =2{y}^{2}-16y+34.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(y)=2{y}^{2}-16y+34.$
